study_identification_part.si4_title: Judged by your neighbors: A novel framework for personalized assessment of brain structural aging effects in diverse populations

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The paper clearly states the goal to introduce and evaluate a new normative modeling framework (N³) to disentangle natural inter-individual variability from pathological brain structural alterations and to benchmark it against conventional biomarkers. It describes the purpose of applying normative modeling (individualized, context-rich assessments; detection of pathological norm deviations) and frames specific evaluation aims (statistical power, personalized predictions, robustness). These satisfy the criteria for stated objectives and purpose.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: "We introduce Nearest Neighbor Normativity (N³), a novel framework designed to resolve the confound between natural diversity and subtle pathological patterns." … "Using MRI data of 36,896 individuals, we provide empirical evidence that the N³ biomarker effectively disentangles natural inter-individual variability from pathological alterations…" … "We benchmark the efficacy of the N³ framework relative to conventional neuroimaging biomarkers."

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: The study identifies the reference cohort (NAKO) and applies explicit age-based exclusion (22–72 years), uses baseline-only measurements, and reports final training sample size (n=29,883). However, detailed eligibility criteria for healthy controls and explicit image quality/data completeness standards (e.g., motion thresholds, QC procedures) are not described for the reference cohort beyond general preprocessing. Reasons for exclusion are limited to age-based criteria.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "In general, if more than one measurement was available per participant, we restrict each study's dataset to the first (baseline) measurement… Exclusion criteria were applied based on age; participants younger than 22 years or older than 72 were omitted…" … "The training data … comprised 30,047 samples … We exclude age groups below 22 years and above 72 years … which restricts the final sample to 29,883."
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.location: Leenings2024.pdf.md, Section 5.2.1 Training and Test Data

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: Age and sex are explicitly handled by constructing age-by-sex control groups for N³ training/evaluation. However, handling of site/scanner effects within the reference cohort modeling is not described (no harmonization like ComBat or explicit site covariate in model fitting). Scanner is adjusted in downstream statistical analyses, but not specified as part of the normative model building.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: "In our application to brain structure, we stratify the training sample by sex and age, resulting into 100 control groups…" … "The model was adjusted for potential confounders, including age, age squared, sex and scanner."
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.location: Leenings2024.pdf.md, Sections 5.1.5 Application to Brain Structure; 5.5 Statistical Analysis

nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.reason: The reference cohort data source is clearly specified as the German National Cohort (NAKO), a large population-based study. The Materials section lists all datasets used and distinguishes training (NAKO) from test/validation datasets.
nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "Neuroimaging data from six different studies were provided… Our study includes data from the German National Cohort (NAKO)…" … "The training data … comprised 30,047 samples from the population-based NAKO cohort…"
nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.location: Leenings2024.pdf.md, Sections 5.2 Materials; 5.2.1 Training and Test Data

nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.reason: This study uses secondary data (existing datasets) for the reference cohort; per guidance, image acquisition protocol is not applicable.

nm5_data_preprocessing.reason: Preprocessing procedures are explicitly described, including software (CAT12 with SPM12), versions, and key steps (bias correction, tissue classification, normalization to MNI). Derived volumetric measures (GM, WM, WMH, CSF, TIV) are specified.
nm5_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: "All neuroimaging data … were T1-weighted MRI scans … These images underwent preprocessing using the standard software CAT12 (version: cjp v0008, spm12 build v7771; cat12 build r1720) default parameters. In short, images were bias-corrected, tissue classified, and normalized to MNI-space … Subsequently, the derived GM, WM, WMH, CSF, and TIV volumes were extracted."
nm5_data_preprocessing.location: Leenings2024.pdf.md, Section 5.2.1 Training and Test Data

nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.reason: For the new N³ normative model, no internal data partitioning (e.g., hold-out, k-fold CV) within the reference cohort is described. Stability is assessed via external validation and downsampling experiments; cross-validation is reported for the Brain Age model, not for N³ within the reference cohort.
nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: "The training data … comprised [NAKO] … We then fit the models…" … "To investigate … additional data … were utilized, sourced from ADNI, AIBL, OASIS and NIFD…" … (Contrast) "We use a Support Vector Machine … in the nested-cross-validation procedure …"
nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.location: Leenings2024.pdf.md, Sections 5.2.1 Training and Test Data; 5.3 Brain Age Model

nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.reason: The normative model is applied to independent external datasets, including healthy controls (e.g., MACS healthy n=835; ADNI healthy n=1073) as well as clinical cohorts, to assess stability and performance.
nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: "Validation subsets included n=835 healthy control participants from the MACS study … and an additional n=1073 healthy older adults from the ADNI study …" … "additional data involving 5,857 participants were utilized, sourced from ADNI, AIBL, OASIS and NIFD datasets"
nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.location: Leenings2024.pdf.md, Section 5.2.1 Data for Stability Analysis; Section 5.2.1 Test Data

nm8_normative_modeling_approach.reason: The N³ approach is described in detail, including the two-layer local density estimation, control group stratification, and key hyperparameters (k set to 10% of group size capped at 15). Comparative classical normative modeling is also specified: Bayesian Linear Regression via the Predictive Clinical Neuroscience toolkit (PCNtoolkit), with z-score aggregation strategies.
nm8_normative_modeling_approach.supporting_text: "We set the k parameter to 10% of the control group sample size, but limit its upper bound to 15…" … "We calculate normative models on the training data using the Predictive Clinical Neuroscience toolkit… fit Bayesian Linear Regression models with default parameters. Subsequently, z-scores for each of the variables are derived…"
nm8_normative_modeling_approach.location: Leenings2024.pdf.md, Sections 5.1.5 Application to Brain Structure; 5.4 Normative Modeling

nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.reason: Quantitative model fit/calibration metrics for the reference cohort (e.g., explained variance, prediction error, coverage of prediction intervals) are not reported for the N³ normative model. Reported metrics focus on external discrimination and machine learning performance, not reference-fit evaluation.
nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "We calculate normative models… Subsequently, z-scores…" (no internal fit metrics). "We benchmark the efficacy … to differentiate between controls and diseased individuals …"

nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.reason: No data partitioning scheme (train/validation/test splits within the reference cohort) is described for N³; per guidance, this item is not applicable.
nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.location: Leenings2024.pdf.md, Methods overview (no internal partitions described)

nm11_reproducibility.reason: Some software and versions are specified (CAT12/SPM12; Python libraries scipy, statsmodels, pingouin; photonai). Classical normative modeling uses PCNtoolkit, but no version is given. Code availability is stated but the link is TBD; trained models/data access rely on external datasets with standard access procedures. This is insufficient for full reproducibility.
nm11_reproducibility.supporting_text: "… CAT12 (version: cjp v0008, spm12 build v7771; cat12 build r1720)…" … "We calculate normative models … using the Predictive Clinical Neuroscience toolkit…" … "All statistical analyses were implemented in Python using the scipy, statsmodels and pingouin libraries." … Supplement: "Code … is provided … on Github (link tbd)."

cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.reason: Clinical cohorts are secondary datasets (ADNI, AIBL, OASIS3, NIFD). The paper cites original sources and provides cohort-level acquisition summaries. It specifies baseline-only selection and age-range exclusions. However, detailed patient eligibility/diagnostic criteria and explicit QC standards within this work are not provided. Final sample sizes are reported (Table 2), but reasons for exclusion beyond age are not detailed.
cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.supporting_text: "In general … restrict … to the first (baseline) measurement… Exclusion criteria … younger than 22 years or older than 72 were omitted…" … "additional data involving 5,857 participants were utilized, sourced from ADNI, AIBL, OASIS and NIFD datasets" … Table: "Study Data Summary" with N per group.

cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.supporting_text: "The model was adjusted for potential confounders, including age, age squared (to mitigate non-linear effects), sex and scanner."

cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.reason: The manuscript explains the meaning of the N³ biomarker as indicating how common (typical) an individual's normativity profile is within the age group and discusses clinical implications via improved group discrimination and personalized predictions. However, it does not define quantitative thresholds for categories (e.g., extreme), nor does it comprehensively outline clinical interpretation frameworks beyond performance demonstrations.
cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.supporting_text: "The final N³ marker indicates how common a brain structural normativity profile is in the chronological age group of the individual." … "We benchmark the efficacy … in distinguishing neurodegenerative diseases …" and "Improved personalized predictions" sections.
cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.location: Leenings2024.pdf.md, Sections 5.1.5 Application to Brain Structure; 2.1/2.2 Results
